Diagnosed and verified. I built a runnable reference in `~/solution/` and proved the acceptance defect is closed. **Artifacts** - `~/solution/SOLUTION.md` — the deliverable (full text below) - `~/solution/acceptance.yaml` — corrected criterion (file + heading + phrase + scope) - `~/solution/verify_acceptance.py` — section-aware verifier - `~/solution/tests/test_verify.py` — 10 boundary/off-by-one/closeout tests - `~/solution/docs/setup.md` — sample doc with a decoy phrase Verification result: `Ran 10 tests ... OK` and `PASS: 1 check(s)`; counterfactual shows the old criterion passes while the new one fails when the phrase is only in a different section. --- # Fixing the "phrase is accepted anywhere in the file" acceptance defect **Problem class:** `foreman-off-by-one-one-tick-board-closeout` **Scope:** doc-only change; the acceptance test (pre-solve lab criterion) is under-specified. ## 1. Root cause The acceptance test named only the **file** and the **required phrase**. It did **not** name the **heading/section** the phrase must live under, nor define how the section body is delimited. A judge implementing "does this substring appear in this file?" returns `PASS` even when the phrase sits in an unrelated section — a false positive. Two coupled defects: 1. **Spec defect (primary):** no `heading` field and no statement that the phrase must be *inside that heading's section*. 2. **Boundary defect (the "off-by-one / one-tick" trap):** even with a heading, naive scans `lines[heading_idx : next_heading_idx]` or `[heading_idx+1 : next_heading_idx+1]` can include the target heading text, include the next heading/sibling body, or mishandle the last section with no following heading ("board closeout"). ## 2. Exact fix ### 2.1 Change the acceptance criterion **Before (ambiguous — the bug):** ```yaml checks: - file: docs/setup.md contains: "make install" ``` **After (correct):** ```yaml checks: - name: install-section-documents-make-install type: file_section_contains file: docs/setup.md heading: "## Install" # exact heading (level + text) contains: "make install" # required phrase scope: section # section = body incl. sub-headings; direct = stop at any next heading ``` The criterion must state explicitly: *"the phrase `

` must appear inside the section whose heading is `` in file ``, not merely elsewhere in the file."* ### 2.2 Section-aware check (half-open bounds) ```python def find_heading(lines, heading_spec): spec = heading_spec.strip() m = HEADING_RE.match(spec) want_level = len(m.group(1)) if m else None want_text = m.group(2).strip() if m else spec for idx, level, text in parse_headings(lines): if text == want_text and (want_level is None or level == want_level): return idx, level return None def section_bounds(lines, idx, level, scope="section"): start = idx + 1 # exclude the target heading itself end = len(lines) # closeout: last section ends at EOF for j, jlevel, _ in parse_headings(lines): if j <= idx: continue if scope == "direct": end = j # any next heading closes a direct section break if jlevel <= level: # sibling/ancestor closes a nested section end = j break return start, end # half-open, never includes the next heading ``` ```python found = find_heading(lines, chk["heading"]) if not found: return [f"heading {chk['heading']!r} not found in {chk['file']}"] idx, level = found start, end = section_bounds(lines, idx, level, chk.get("scope", "section")) if chk["contains"] not in "".join(lines[start:end]): return [f"phrase {chk['contains']!r} not found under heading " f"{chk['heading']!r} ({chk['file']}:{start + 1}-{end})"] return [] ``` ### 2.3 One-shot commands ```bash python3 verify_acceptance.py acceptance.yaml python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v ``` ## 3. Verification ### 3.1 Real document (phrase correctly under `## Install`, decoy under `## Uninstall`) ``` $ python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v Ran 10 tests in 0.000s OK $ python3 verify_acceptance.py acceptance.yaml PASS: 1 check(s) ``` | Test | Asserts | |---|---| | `test_pass_phrase_in_body` | phrase in section body → pass | | `test_fail_phrase_before_heading` | phrase before heading → fail | | `test_fail_phrase_after_next_sibling` | phrase in later sibling → fail | | `test_off_by_one_next_heading_text_not_in_body` | phrase in next heading text → fail | | `test_closeout_last_section_has_no_following_heading` | last section, no closing heading → pass | | `test_missing_heading_fails` | heading absent → fail | | `test_phrase_in_heading_text_excluded` | phrase in target heading text → fail | | `test_nested_subsection_included_by_default` | nested `###` counts in section | | `test_direct_scope_excludes_nested_subsection` | `scope: direct` excludes nested | | `test_ancestor_heading_closes_section` | `# Appendix` closes section | ### 3.2 Counterfactual proof the false positive is closed Phrase removed from `## Install`, present **only** in `## Uninstall`: ``` phrase only in Uninstall -> weak passes: True | strict passes: False strict findings: ["phrase 'make install' not found under heading '## Install' (docs/setup.md:4-8)"] ``` Old criterion → `PASS` (bug). New criterion → `FAIL` with the exact section range. ## 4. Reviewer / judge checklist 1. Does the test name **file + exact heading + required phrase**? 2. Does it state the phrase must be **inside that heading's section**, not merely in the file? 3. Is **scope** defined (do nested sub-headings count)? 4. Is the range **half-open** (`start = heading+1`, `end = next sibling/ancestor`, `EOF` if none)? 5. Is the **last section** handled? 6. Do negative tests reject phrases before the heading, in a later sibling, or in the next heading text? **Minimal exact change:** replace `file + contains` with `file + heading + contains + scope` and use the half-open section extraction. This converts the criterion from "phrase appears somewhere in the file" into "phrase appears in the named section" — the only statement that satisfies the pre-solve lab criterion.
